about: Events an onboarding agent can hit, each mapped to what to do and where the runbook covers it (R6). Keys are <phase>.<event>. When an event happens, read its entry, then its runbook section; if guidance/<key>.md exists in this starter, read that too. An entry's report says which phase and outcome to report when the event ends the phase.

prerequisites.no-gateway.trigger: No gateway URL was given, and .pcc/base does not exist.
prerequisites.no-gateway.do: Ask the human which PCC gateway to use (class C). Never guess one, and never use production unless told to.

prerequisites.gateway-unreachable.trigger: GET <gateway>/api/health does not answer 200 with JSON.
prerequisites.gateway-unreachable.do: Stop and report what you saw. Don't try another address.

prerequisites.no-crypto.trigger: import nacl.signing fails, or pcc-node refuses with LogSigningRefused or mentions pynacl.
prerequisites.no-crypto.do: Install pcc-node with the crypto extra. Without it the node can never sign evidence, so its work can never verify.

prerequisites.key-leaked.trigger: An API key, a .pcc header file or a private key was printed, pasted into the conversation, or committed.
prerequisites.key-leaked.do: Tell the human. Provision a new key (phase 0 step 4, same email) and rewrite .pcc/api-key and .pcc/auth.header. Then revoke the leaked key: find its id with GET /api/auth/keys (match its prefix) and send DELETE /api/auth/keys/<id> with the new key. Never repeat the leaked value.
prerequisites.key-leaked.section: 4. An operator API key, captured without logging it

identify.device-unreachable.trigger: The device does not answer at the recorded address.
identify.device-unreachable.do: Check that the address includes its port and that the device is on. Ask the human only to power it up or give its address.

identify.device-unknown.trigger: Neither the device's own API, nor its manual, nor its label names the make and model.
identify.device-unknown.do: Describe it to POST /api/onboard/identify-device, or send a photo. Pass on only the clarifying questions you can't answer yourself.
identify.device-unknown.section: 2. If the device can't say what it is

intake.dont-know.trigger: The human answers "don't know" to a class C question.
intake.dont-know.do: Don't press. Treat it as class B: research it, then propose a value with its source for the human to confirm. Money and safety are never defaulted.

intake.asks-about-pay.trigger: The human asks how prices, payouts, fees or contributor pay work.
intake.asks-about-pay.do: Answer from the runbook. The price is theirs to set. PCC cannot yet pay a wallet they name, so this runbook runs test jobs only and nothing is paid out yet. Publishing a kit adds a license that the buyer pays on top (phase 8). Quote no number that isn't in the runbook or the gateway.
intake.asks-about-pay.section: How contributor pay works (tell the human this before they choose)

intake.asks-about-safety.trigger: The human asks what the emergency stop, supervision or limits mean.
intake.asks-about-safety.do: A physical stop is required; PCC's remote stop is best effort, not a safety device. Every limit comes from a cited source, or from the human, and the human confirms the envelope once.

research.sources-conflict.trigger: Two sources, or a source and the human's answer, give different values for the same quantity.
research.sources-conflict.do: Don't pick one. List both with their citations and ask the human.

research.no-citation.trigger: A limit, input range or output you need has no unit or no citation.
research.no-citation.do: It cannot become a limit yet. Research it with the ready-to-fire prompts, or ask the human for a value they confirm.

build.envelope-edited.trigger: The human changes a value in the safety envelope, or the envelope changes after it was confirmed.
build.envelope-edited.do: Re-check the value's unit and source, show the changed lines, and record a new confirmation with the new digest. Never run under an envelope the human hasn't confirmed.
build.envelope-edited.section: 3. The safety envelope: draft, then one confirmation (R8)

register.refused.trigger: A register call (kernel, signing key, capability, device or channel) answers 4xx.
register.refused.do: Read the {error, message} body and fix what it names. Report the route and the status, never a key.

register.signing-refused.trigger: register_signing_key refuses with LogSigningRefused, or mentions pynacl.
register.signing-refused.do: Install the crypto extra, delete .pcc/node-keys.json and .pcc/node-public-key, run phase 0 step 3 again, then the signing step.

verify.job-missing.trigger: Once a queue-only submission exists: the test job never shows up in GET /api/operator/jobs for your kernel.
verify.job-missing.do: Check that the submit answered with a jobId and that the job names your kernel, then report it. Don't fall back to /api/setup/test-job: it runs on a built-in mock device.
verify.job-missing.section: 3. Run it the way the operating loop will (phase 7), once, by hand

verify.params-refused.trigger: A job's parameters fail the type check or the envelope check.
verify.params-refused.do: Don't touch the device. Set the job's status to failed with the reason.

verify.device-busy.trigger: The device reports busy or estopped when a job is due to run.
verify.device-busy.do: Don't run it, and don't queue over it. Try again later, and report it if it stays busy.
verify.device-busy.section: 3. Run it the way the operating loop will (phase 7), once, by hand

verify.estop-drill-failed.trigger: During the drill the stop did not read STOPPED, or the device did not stop on its own command.
verify.estop-drill-failed.do: Stop onboarding and report exactly what happened. Clear the stop only after the human confirms the device is safe.
verify.estop-drill-failed.section: 1. Read the stop, and drill it, before anything runs

operate.paid-job-refused.trigger: A job's GET /api/jobs/<jobId>/settlement shows a negotiation session or an escrow: it carries money.
operate.paid-job-refused.do: Don't run it. Send failed with reason payout_destination_unbound, and report it: PCC cannot yet pay a wallet the human confirmed.

operate.estop-active.trigger: GET /api/operator/policy/<kernelId> shows emergencyStop: true, answers with the gateway's default policy (source "default", no updatedAt), or cannot be read.
operate.estop-active.do: Take no job this round. On entering the state, send the device its stop once. Resume only after the human clears the stop.

operate.device-down.trigger: The device stops answering, or its consumables run out.
operate.device-down.do: Stop taking jobs, and say so in the capability description or with the emergency stop. Report it.

publish.asks-about-license.trigger: The human asks what a kit license is, or what rate to choose.
publish.asks-about-license.do: Explain it: 0-100 bps of each job's gross, 50 by default, 0 allowed, paid by the buyer on top, and shared with upstream kits when forked. Pay is shown in test mode for now. The rate is theirs to choose.
publish.asks-about-license.section: How contributor pay works (tell the human this before they choose)

session.stopping-early.trigger: You are blocked, the human stops, or you run out of budget.
session.stopping-early.do: Send the session report anyway, with abandoned or budget_stop, saying where and why.

verify.test-job-blocked.trigger: The gateway offers no server-enforced queue-only submission (true of every current gateway).
verify.test-job-blocked.do: Don't submit a test job: /api/jobs/submit can start it on the gateway's own devices before any check. Report verify blocked; the drill's result stands.
verify.test-job-blocked.section: 2. The test job: blocked on the current gateway

verify.stop-not-clear.trigger: The stop does not read CLEAR after the drill's resume, or immediately before a run.
verify.stop-not-clear.do: Don't submit and don't run. Report what the policy read showed.
verify.stop-not-clear.section: 1. Read the stop, and drill it, before anything runs

verify.money-attached.trigger: Once a queue-only submission exists: the test job's GET /api/jobs/<jobId>/settlement shows a session or an escrow.
verify.money-attached.do: Don't run it: it is not a test job. Report what the settlement showed.
verify.money-attached.section: 2. The test job: blocked on the current gateway

verify.evidence-not-stored.trigger: POST /api/operator/evidence answered without "stored": true for this jobId (HTTP 200 included).
verify.evidence-not-stored.do: Send status failed with reason evidence_not_stored, never completed, and report what the receipt said.
verify.evidence-not-stored.section: 3. Run it the way the operating loop will (phase 7), once, by hand
